note: Study skeleton paraphrased from the course scope (not verbatim College Board prose; unit numbers are our own sequencing, not official CED numbers). Skill codes are indicative: 1.x concept, 2.x/3.x skill.

objectives.statement: Explain position, velocity, and acceleration as derivatives and integrals of each other.
Solve motion problems by differentiating and integrating, including non-constant acceleration.
Explain dynamics with calculus-based force analysis including drag and variable forces.
Set up and solve differential relationships in Newton's second law problems.
Explain work as a line integral and power as the rate of energy transfer.
Apply conservation of energy with calculus-based potential functions.
Explain impulse as an integral and momentum conservation in collisions.
Solve variable-mass and multi-body collision problems.
Explain torque, moment of inertia via integration, and angular momentum.
Solve rotational dynamics problems using calculus where mass distributions vary.
Explain Newton's law of gravitation, orbital motion, and gravitational potential energy.
Calculate orbital speeds, periods, and escape velocities.
Explain simple harmonic motion as a second-order differential equation.
Solve SHM systems including pendulums and springs with calculus methods.
